title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: inverse-class parallel rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^127.36 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000). It computes g=e(P,Q0) and then solves z=g^a by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on inverse classes {x,x^-1}, where inversion in GT is the p^6-power conjugation. Under the stated random-mapping heuristic, supported by toy experiments, the success probability is at least 0.39. The budget is 1.25*sqrt(2*N*ln(1/0.61)) useful steps on N=(r+1)/2 classes, times 1.03 for abandoned fruitless-cycle walks, at 1.05 units per step, plus additive setup, distinguished-point lag, storage and output costs below 2^-20 of the main term. Peak memory is at most 2^114 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^25 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. It is a generic accounting, not a novel attack or practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run parallel distinguished-point rho on inverse classes in a prime-order subgroup of F_q^*, with look-ahead and stuck-walk restarts. Count all steps and report the mean steps relative to sqrt(pi*l/4) and the success rate within the claimed 1.25*k0 budget. Toy-scale evidence for the random-mapping heuristic only.
